note: Exhausted by the end, and sweated a lot more than normal.
Lower back strain noticed the following day. Trap bar and Smith squat sets are the likely source; nothing was felt during the session itself.

First session back after two rest days for the lower back strain. Cable row cut and pullups taken to three sets to carry the pulling volume; lat pulldown kept because no chest-supported row was free. Standing curls and standing 15 lb Y raises were forced by equipment, and both put the low back to work stabilising.
Sled only, on the fourth day after the lower-back strain and the first morning the back felt normal. Tiring and a heavy sweat despite no lifting, which is what fifty minutes at full resistance buys.

One full-body session, the only day this week training was possible -- sled, jumps, trap bar, bench, pullups, squat and dips. Pullups came before the squat rather than after, the one departure that was not forced. The result is the trap bar: 240 for two sets of five, reported quite easy, eight days after the session the lower-back strain followed and with nothing from the back this time. Bench was 150 rather than 155 only because the plates were not there. Pullups quite hard, taken fifth. Upper traps worked hard, and recurring.

The away-from-the-gym routine -- all seven daily items at the prescribed doses, fifteen minutes against its stated twelve. No bells on the trip, so the four bell slots show as missed; they were substituted, not skipped. Of the foot block, only the supinated calf raise was done, folded into the calf raises as an outside-edge bias.
The away routine again -- all seven items, fifteen minutes. Bell slots missed for want of bells, as on the 15th. The foot block was not reported either way and is not claimed.

The away routine, reported a day late as "the away routine thing" and nothing more, so the set rows carry its prescribed doses rather than a report and no duration was given. Bell slots missed for want of bells.

The away routine, fourth run of the trip. Reported as "a stretch session" and nothing more, so the set rows carry its prescribed doses rather than a report and no duration was given. Bell slots missed for want of bells.

First heavy lower in fifteen days. Two stations were unavailable -- the Smith machine taken, the lying leg curl machine broken -- and the sled was gone by the end, so all three deviations are equipment rather than choices. Trap bar 260 for a clean 2x5, medium-hard with room left: the pre-trip weight recovered in full. Exhausted straight after the deadlifts and recovered by the end, lower back fine and still fine in the evening, so the fatigue 3 is the shape of the session rather than its peak. Sweat reported as a decent amount; duration not recorded.

The pullup test the plan asks for every few weeks, and it paid: 8 reps against the 7 of Aug 1, a new best and the goal now 8 of 10. It cost the rest of the session, which is the trade a real all-out set makes -- the second pullup set fell to 3 and bench went 8, 7, then 3 at 130, cooked after the first set, for 18 reps against the prescribed 24. Both pulls ran as written for the first time since the back strain, at 130 apiece, and the preacher and seated Y raise got their programmed bench versions back after Aug 8's forced standing substitutes. Cable fly and dips were lost to time, the fly being optional and dips already at target. Worth noting the fuel: 455 kcal all day before this, a protein bar and twelve Sour Patch Kids, which is a thin base for a max-effort set.

Light shooting around, reported as "a bit of light basketball" with no duration given and nothing countable, so every column but the date and the type is blank. Its own row because basketball is its own session type, and it draws no plan comparison by design; no set rows exist for it, which also keeps it out of the light upper's session card. Note that the dashboard shows one session a day via sessionOn(), so on the 22nd only the light upper renders and this row is currently data without a view.

The first light lower in the log, so the first session the program's light-lower day has ever been graded against. Two deviations, both ordering rather than content: the jumps came after the lifts instead of first and fresh, and the depth jumps came after the weighted jumps rather than before, which inverts the plan's one stated ordering rule -- the sled being rained off is the third and was not a choice. The lower back that was sore this morning felt fine throughout, which answers the gate this session was run under. Every load was reported quite easy -- 210 trap bar, 150 Smith, a first-ever 110 leg curl -- but the session itself felt lethargic and the brunch is named as the cause, 1,517 kcal and 118 g of sugar of it. Fatigue was first written 2 from the ease of the loads and is now 3, because the lethargy is what this column records and the loads are already carried as weights.

The heavy upper the Aug 25 note was waiting on, and the first heavy upper since Aug 4 -- three rest days since the Aug 23 light lower. Bench 160 x 5 is the headline: a 5 lb step on the Aug 4 top set, the heaviest bench actually performed in the log, and reported as not too bad, which puts the stated 165 baseline in front rather than behind. One deviation and it was equipment -- the 20 lb dumbbells were gone, so the seated Y raise became a cable lateral raise at 12.5 lbs for 4 and 3, well under the 2 x 5. Everything else ran as written: pullups 2 x 5 at the top of the range, cable row 2 x 5 at 130, preacher curl 6 then 4 for the same ten reps at 25, both sled bouts, and dips back at 1 x 10 after the 7 of Aug 4 and the Aug 22 miss. Fatigue 4, reported after the fact -- fine through the session and very tired right at the end, the opposite shape to the Aug 20 heavy lower, which peaked early and recovered. The pullups came with it: 2 x 5 went up but felt quite hard, four days after the all-out 8. Sixty-five minutes.

The first heavy lower to run exactly as written -- every slot filled, both sled bouts, and none of the equipment deviations that shaped Aug 5 and Aug 20. Trap bar 270 for 2x5 is the headline: a 10 lb step on the 260 held since Aug 1, double the plan's 2.5-5 lb rule and 5 over what the Aug 20 note called for, and it puts the lift about 3 lbs ahead of the pace line to 300 for the first time. Smith squat 175 finally landed as a clean 2x5 after the 5-then-4 of Aug 5, and the leg curl took 120. Traps reported as pinching on the deadlift and a better warmup asked for -- the first trap report anywhere in the log, two days after the heaviest bench in it and the shoulder-and-chest soreness that followed, so it is flagged rather than written off; both main lifts felt not horrendous but definitely tired, hence fatigue 3.
